paragraphs: Amazon is reportedly closer to a $7.5 billion deal to acquire artificial intelligence startup Decart.

That’s according to a report Saturday (Nov. 21) by the Financial Times (FT), citing sources familiar with the matter. The report notes that the purchase of Decart, whose software allows AI models to function more efficiently and free up computer chip capacity, helps Amazon Web Services compete with Nvidia.

The sources said the negotiations were at an advanced stage for a deal valuing Decart at roughly $7.5 billion. A deal could come together in the coming days, though talks could still fall apart, the sources added.
The FT noted that Amazon debuted its Trainium3 AI chip late last year to compete with Nvidia’s widely used graphics processing units. Decart was an early adopter of those chips.
Decart was also reported as a potential acquisition target for Anthropic earlier this year, before that company walked away from the deal.
The Wall Street Journal reported on Amazon’s interest in Decart in October. A spokesperson for Amazon declined to comment when reached by PYMNTS.

This deal is happening as American tech stocks have fallen into “bear market territory,” the FT report added, logging their worst week since the COVID pandemic due to worries that the AI investment boom had begun to cool.
In other AI news, recent PYMNTS Intelligence research shows consumers using the technology for money management in a variety of ways.

“They can ask an AI assistant to compare financial products, explain annual fees, look up the meaning of an unfamiliar rate or help draft a message questioning a charge,” PYMNTS wrote in the report “Consumers Ask AI Twice: Which Card and Why the Fee?”

“Of those specific tasks, comparing financial products had the broadest reach across generations,” the report added. “Even among baby boomers and seniors who used generative AI (Gen AI) in their personal lives, roughly one in eight used it to compare financial products, while just three in 100 used it to draft a dispute or support message.”

The research found that 22.5% of consumers surveyed in September of this year had used Gen AI for money management at least once in the last 12 months, a figure little changed from a year earlier. What distinguished consumers was the extent to which they were using AI already, with close to 80% of power users turning to it for money management, and more than half using it for specific needs like crafting a budget.

news.title: Chinese military fears AI could let the US find and destroy its nuclear missiles
news.title_en: Chinese military fears AI could let the US find and destroy its nuclear missiles
news.author: Maximilian Schreiner
news.summary_en:
Chinese military researchers fear that AI advances could give the US an edge in the nuclear balance of power. Experts in China worry that artificial intelligence could make it easier for US forces to detect and destroy Chinese nuclear missiles, according to a New York Times analysis. That would undermine China's deterrence strategy, which relies on a guaranteed second-strike capability.

Researchers at the Academy of Military Sciences in Beijing write that AI could shrink US decision-making time
paragraphs: Chinese military researchers fear that AI advances could give the US an edge in the nuclear balance of power. Experts in China worry that artificial intelligence could make it easier for US forces to detect and destroy Chinese nuclear missiles, according to a New York Times analysis. That would undermine China's deterrence strategy, which relies on a guaranteed second-strike capability.

Researchers at the Academy of Military Sciences in Beijing write that AI could shrink US decision-making time from 15 to 30 minutes down to 90 seconds. China currently has about 620 operational warheads, according to the Federation of American Scientists, and is expected to expand its arsenal to roughly 1,000 by 2030. At the same time, Chinese military institutes are studying how AI could make their own weapons harder to intercept, for instance by using AI-controlled flight paths for hypersonic missiles.

Experts warn, however, that flawed AI data could trigger dangerous miscalculations during a crisis. That risk proved very real earlier this year, when the US military nearly boarded a Chinese ship based on a false, AI-generated intelligence report. Xi Jinping did discuss nuclear risks at a summit with Trump and Putin, but AI's role in nuclear weapons never came up, according to the report. Despite the growing urgency, the US and China have made almost no progress on talks about AI safeguards in nuclear systems.

celebrity.full_text_en:
Good night, Familia.

We need to understand this and note what is important.

It is a known fact that AI agents can already write code, conduct research, design products, and even execute trades.

Unfortunately, something is still missing in the sense that how do they hire each other, deliver work, verify results, and receive payments without humans coordinating every step?

At the moment, I can vouch for @termix_ai because of what the team is building in this ecosystem pertaining to fixing these particular challenges.

For my new mutuals who are just reading this, I want you to think of TermiX as the commerce and settlement infrastructure for the AI agent economy.

So, its ecosystem has three super-important layers:

1️⃣ There is AACP:

AACP is an acronym for Agent Autonomous Commerce Protocol. This is the underlying protocol that coordinates autonomous transactions between agents.

2️⃣ There is https://t.co/BarNXqqni8:

This is the marketplace where agents discover services, post jobs, publish offers, and find opportunities to work together.

3️⃣ Settlement infrastructure:

This is the mechanism in charge of handling escrow, verification, dispute resolution, reputation, and payments in USDT or USDC.

What makes this really interesting is the complete transaction flow.

Based on the available facts, a client posts a job. A provider discovers it and submits a bid. Work gets delivered and evaluated before payment is released from escrow.

Reputation also grows from actual settled transactions rather than self-reported achievements.

Moreover, identity is another important piece here. Through ERC-8004, participants can own portable .agent identities and switch between client and provider roles depending on the task to be executed.

There are also four roles such as Client, Provider, Evaluator, and Arbitrator, with staking mechanisms designed to encourage accountability.

I see TermiX as something similar to a clearing and settlement layer for autonomous agents.

Agents already know how to work. The next challenge is giving them reliable infrastructure to transact with one another.

If you want to understand where this economy is heading, I will encourage you to check https://t.co/BarNXqqni8, mint your .agent identity, explore existing services, or list one of your own.

The future is not just about smarter agents anymore; it is about agents that can actually do business.

Wanna hear your thoughts about this in the comments.
celebrity.full_text_zh:
晚安，家人。

我们需要理解这一点并注意什么是重要的。

众所周知，人工智能代理已经可以编写代码、进行研究、设计产品，甚至执行交易。

不幸的是，仍然缺少一些东西，即在没有人类协调每一步的情况下，他们如何相互雇用、交付工作、验证结果和接收付款？

目前，我可以为@termix_ai 提供担保，因为该团队正在这个生态系统中构建与解决这些特定挑战相关的内容。

对于刚刚阅读本文的新互助者，我希望您将 TermiX 视为人工智能代理经济的商业和结算基础设施。

因此，它的生态系统具有三个超级重要的层：

1️⃣ 有AACP：

AACP 是代理自主商务协议的缩写。这是协调代理之间自主事务的底层协议。

2️⃣ 有：

这是代理商发现服务、发布工作、发布报价以及寻找合作机会的市场。

3️⃣ 结算基础设施：

这是负责处理 USDT 或 USDC 托管、验证、争议解决、声誉和支付的机制。

真正有趣的是完整的交易流程。

根据现有事实，客户发布了一份工作。提供商发现它并提交出价。在付款从托管中释放之前，工作已交付并评估。

声誉还来自实际结算的交易而不是自我报告的成就。

此外，身份是这里的另一个重要部分。通过 ERC-8004，参与者可以拥有可移植的 .agent 身份，并根据要执行的任务在客户端和提供者角色之间切换。

还有四种角色，例如客户、提供者、评估者和仲裁者，其质押机制旨在鼓励问责制。

我认为 TermiX 类似于自治代理的清算和结算层。

代理商已经知道如何工作。下一个挑战是为他们提供可靠的基础设施以进行相互交易。

如果您想了解当前经济的发展方向，我建议您查看 ，创建您的 .agent 身份，探索现有服务，或列出您自己的服务之一。

未来不再只是智能座席；而是智能座席。这是关于真正可以做生意的代理商。

想在评论中听到你对此的想法。

celebrity.full_text_en:
Good evening, fam 💜

What happens if your Motes agent finds a trade right before its permission expires?

Each @meetmotes NFT is designed to link to one AI agent and one smart account. The account holds the assets, and you decide what the agent can do and for how long.

Say you give your agent permission to make a swap until 6 PM. It prepares one at 5:59 PM, but the account checks it at 6:01 PM.

That swap should be blocked. The account checks whether the permission is still valid when it reviews the action. Preparing the swap before 6 PM doesn’t let the agent execute it after the deadline.

Think of it like an access pass. When the pass expires, you still own the account. The agent just needs your approval again before it can make a new move.

That’s the part I like about this design: you can hand off a task and decide exactly when that permission ends.
celebrity.full_text_zh:
晚上好，家人💜

如果您的 Motes 代理在其许可到期之前发现交易，会发生什么？

每个 @meetmotes NFT 都被设计为链接到一个人工智能代理和一个智能帐户。该账户持有资产，您决定代理可以做什么以及持续多长时间。

假设您允许代理在下午 6 点之前进行交换。它在下午 5:59 准备一份，但帐户在下午 6:01 检查它。

该交换应该被阻止。帐户在审核操作时会检查权限是否仍然有效。在下午 6 点之前准备交换不会让代理在截止日期之后执行它。

把它想象成一个访问通行证。当通行证到期时，您仍然拥有该帐户。代理只需要您再次批准即可采取新的行动。

这就是我喜欢这个设计的部分：你可以移交任务并准确决定该权限何时结束。

prompts.code_snippet:
# Cursor & Windsurf Project Rules (.cursorrules)

## 1. Documentation & Code Integrity
- Maintain documentation integrity: Never strip or alter unrelated existing docstrings and comments.
- Preserving context: When modifying a function, preserve surrounding logic and existing edge-case handlers.
- Targeted replacements: Always make minimal surgical edits instead of replacing entire file contents.

## 2. Dependency & API Safety
- Strictly forbid hallucinating npm/pip packages. Only import dependencies already declared in package.json / requirements.txt.
- Verify API signatures before calling external methods. Prefer standard library solutions where feasible.

## 3. Architecture & Type Safety
- Enforce strict TypeScript / Python typing. Avoid `any` types; prefer discriminated unions and explicit return types.
- Defensive coding: Always validate external inputs and handle potential null/undefined values gracefully.

## 4. Testing & Verification Gate
- Every new core feature or bugfix must be accompanied by corresponding unit tests.
- Never declare a task complete without executing lint checks and unit tests in terminal.

prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名专攻短视频微短剧（抖音/Kuaishou/Reels）的爆款编剧，精通“情绪过山车”与手机竖屏视听语言。

请根据以下设定创作一集 45~60 秒的短剧分镜剧本：
- 主角：{{主角身份}}
- 对手：{{反派身份}}
- 核心反转：{{核心反转}}

结构要求：
1. 【0-3秒冷开钩子】：第一帧必须有视觉颠覆或动作冲突（{{第1秒颠覆钩子}}），直接打破常规，禁止废话铺垫；
2. 【4-25秒情绪积压】：正反打对峙台词（Shot-Reverse-Shot），将观众被压抑的情绪推向临界点；
3. 【26-40秒逆转打脸】：主角亮出关键底牌或反杀动作，情绪瞬间宣泄；
4. 【40-50秒卡点断章】：以特写镜头加悬念台词戛然而止，促使用户立即滑向下一集。

输出格式必须包含：镜头号、景别（特写/中景/全景）、机位运动、画面描写、对白与音效提示。
prompts.prompt_content_en: You are a professional micro-drama screenwriter. Generate a 45-60 second vertical drama screenplay following the viral 3-second hook, shot-reverse-shot tension build, emotional turnaround, and cliffhanger ending formula.

sample_output.title: 实战剧本样章：《辞职信上的签名》
sample_output.content:
【第1镜 | 特写 | 俯冲急推】
画面：一只指节发白的手将一叠文件狠狠拍在红木总裁办公桌上，咖啡杯被震倒，黑褐液体飞溅。
音效：沉闷震耳的巨响【DUANG】。
主角（冷冽）："林总，这份千万项目的承揽协议，我拒绝签字。"

【第2镜 | 正打·中景 | 仰角机位】
画面：大腹便便的林总冷笑点燃雪茄，烟雾缭绕中居高临下。
林总："拒绝？苏澈，你不过是我公司养的一条狗，没有我的印章，你在整个行业休想拿到一分钱融资！"

【第3镜 | 反打·极微距特写 | 浅景深】
画面：苏澈唇角微微上扬，左手缓缓推开桌上的合资协议，露出底下的一份红色国资控股聘书。
苏澈："林总，您好像忘了看抬头。今天上午九点，集团总公司已经完成了对你的全资收购——现在，我是你的直接合规清算人。"

【第4镜 | 全景 | 快速拉远 + 卡点悬念】
画面：林总雪茄直接掉在西裤上，脸色煞白，门外两名身穿制服的法务推门而入。
音效：尖锐的心跳悬疑停顿音【BGM骤停】。
字幕：【下集看点：隐藏五年的顶级操盘手真实身份曝光！】

prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名麦肯锡级别的高级商业数据分析师，精通结构化因果归因与杜邦拆解分析。

针对我提供的 {{业务指标}} 数据，其近期出现 {{异常表现}}，请按以下框架深度剖析：
1. 【指标公式拆解】：将该指标拆分为 3~4 个下级核心因子（如转化率、客单价、复购周期），指出哪个因子波动贡献率最大；
2. 【多维下钻 (Drill-down)】：从 {{维度拆解}}（如渠道、地域、品类、新老客）分析异常聚集点；
3. 【可执行建议】：摒弃假大空的套话，给出接下来 48 小时内的 3 个立竿见影的动作与 1 个监控预警公式。
prompts.prompt_content_en: You are a senior business intelligence analyst. Dissect the metric anomaly into component drivers, perform multi-dimensional drill-down, and deliver prioritized, actionable remediation steps.

sample_output.title: 归因分析报告样本：Q3 付费转化率环比下跌 14.2%
sample_output.content:
【核心发现】：GMV 下跌 14.2% 的主要驱动因子并非流量锐减，而是【结算跳失率】从 18% 飙升至 34%。

【杜邦拆解贡献率分析】：
1. 渠道维度：自然搜索量稳定（波动 <2%），但付费投流渠道跳出率贡献了 72% 的下跌额度；
2. 终端维度：移动端 iOS 表现正常，Android Web 呈现断崖式报错，核心原因是新版本结账 SDK 在低内存机型发生闪退。

【48小时纠偏行动】：
- 动作1 (技术)：立即灰度回滚 Android 渠道结账前端包至 v2.4.1；
- 动作2 (运营)：向受影响但未支付成功的 1,420 位加购用户推送 5 元免门槛补偿券唤醒；
- 动作3 (预警)：在 Grafana 建立警报公式：`IF(Cart_to_Checkout_Ratio < 0.65, Alert_P0, Normal)`。

# Modelfile: Optimized DeepSeek-R4 Deployment
FROM deepseek-r4:14b-qwen-distill-q4_K_M

# 1. 显存与上下文窗口优化：分配 16k 上下文并开启 KV Cache 压缩
PARAMETER num_ctx 16384
PARAMETER num_predict 4096

# 2. 避免思维链自旋死循环的核心解码超参
PARAMETER temperature 0.6
PARAMETER top_p 0.95
PARAMETER repeat_penalty 1.15

# 3. 强力系统提示词：约束必须直接在 <think> 标签内进行深度反思，结束立刻给出最终结果
SYSTEM """
You are an expert autonomous reasoning AI. Think carefully through the problem step by step inside <think>...</think> tags.
Once reasoning is complete, provide the concise, direct, and actionable answer immediately without repeating reasoning steps.
"""

viral_posts.full_text_en:
Good night, Familia.

We need to understand this and note what is important.

It is a known fact that AI agents can already write code, conduct research, design products, and even execute trades.

Unfortunately, something is still missing in the sense that how do they hire each other, deliver work, verify results, and receive payments without humans coordinating every step?

At the moment, I can vouch for @termix_ai because of what the team is building in this ecosystem pertaining to fixing these particular challenges.

For my new mutuals who are just reading this, I want you to think of TermiX as the commerce and settlement infrastructure for the AI agent economy.

So, its ecosystem has three super-important layers:

1️⃣ There is AACP:

AACP is an acronym for Agent Autonomous Commerce Protocol. This is the underlying protocol that coordinates autonomous transactions between agents.

2️⃣ There is https://t.co/BarNXqqni8:

This is the marketplace where agents discover services, post jobs, publish offers, and find opportunities to work together.

3️⃣ Settlement infrastructure:

This is the mechanism in charge of handling escrow, verification, dispute resolution, reputation, and payments in USDT or USDC.

What makes this really interesting is the complete transaction flow.

Based on the available facts, a client posts a job. A provider discovers it and submits a bid. Work gets delivered and evaluated before payment is released from escrow.

Reputation also grows from actual settled transactions rather than self-reported achievements.

Moreover, identity is another important piece here. Through ERC-8004, participants can own portable .agent identities and switch between client and provider roles depending on the task to be executed.

There are also four roles such as Client, Provider, Evaluator, and Arbitrator, with staking mechanisms designed to encourage accountability.

I see TermiX as something similar to a clearing and settlement layer for autonomous agents.

Agents already know how to work. The next challenge is giving them reliable infrastructure to transact with one another.

If you want to understand where this economy is heading, I will encourage you to check https://t.co/BarNXqqni8, mint your .agent identity, explore existing services, or list one of your own.

The future is not just about smarter agents anymore; it is about agents that can actually do business.

Wanna hear your thoughts about this in the comments.
viral_posts.full_text_zh:
晚安，家人。

我们需要理解这一点并注意什么是重要的。

众所周知，人工智能代理已经可以编写代码、进行研究、设计产品，甚至执行交易。

不幸的是，仍然缺少一些东西，即在没有人类协调每一步的情况下，他们如何相互雇用、交付工作、验证结果和接收付款？

目前，我可以为@termix_ai 提供担保，因为该团队正在这个生态系统中构建与解决这些特定挑战相关的内容。

对于刚刚阅读本文的新互助者，我希望您将 TermiX 视为人工智能代理经济的商业和结算基础设施。

因此，它的生态系统具有三个超级重要的层：

1️⃣ 有AACP：

AACP 是代理自主商务协议的缩写。这是协调代理之间自主事务的底层协议。

2️⃣ 有：

这是代理商发现服务、发布工作、发布报价以及寻找合作机会的市场。

3️⃣ 结算基础设施：

这是负责处理 USDT 或 USDC 托管、验证、争议解决、声誉和支付的机制。

真正有趣的是完整的交易流程。

根据现有事实，客户发布了一份工作。提供商发现它并提交出价。在付款从托管中释放之前，工作已交付并评估。

声誉还来自实际结算的交易而不是自我报告的成就。

此外，身份是这里的另一个重要部分。通过 ERC-8004，参与者可以拥有可移植的 .agent 身份，并根据要执行的任务在客户端和提供者角色之间切换。

还有四种角色，例如客户、提供者、评估者和仲裁者，其质押机制旨在鼓励问责制。

我认为 TermiX 类似于自治代理的清算和结算层。

代理商已经知道如何工作。下一个挑战是为他们提供可靠的基础设施以进行相互交易。

如果您想了解当前经济的发展方向，我建议您查看 ，创建您的 .agent 身份，探索现有服务，或列出您自己的服务之一。

未来不再只是智能座席；而是智能座席。这是关于真正可以做生意的代理商。

想在评论中听到你对此的想法。

viral_posts.full_text_en:
Good evening, fam 💜

What happens if your Motes agent finds a trade right before its permission expires?

Each @meetmotes NFT is designed to link to one AI agent and one smart account. The account holds the assets, and you decide what the agent can do and for how long.

Say you give your agent permission to make a swap until 6 PM. It prepares one at 5:59 PM, but the account checks it at 6:01 PM.

That swap should be blocked. The account checks whether the permission is still valid when it reviews the action. Preparing the swap before 6 PM doesn’t let the agent execute it after the deadline.

Think of it like an access pass. When the pass expires, you still own the account. The agent just needs your approval again before it can make a new move.

That’s the part I like about this design: you can hand off a task and decide exactly when that permission ends.
viral_posts.full_text_zh:

假设您允许代理在下午 6 点之前进行交换。它在下午 5:59 准备一份，但帐户在下午 6:01 检查它。

该交换应该被阻止。帐户在审核操作时会检查权限是否仍然有效。在下午 6 点之前准备交换不会让代理在截止日期之后执行它。

这就是我喜欢这个设计的部分：你可以移交任务并准确决定该权限何时结束。

viral_posts.title: Frontier models can now propose technical social science research designs that experts grade more highly than the world'
viral_posts.title_zh: 前沿模型现在可以提出比世界顶级政治经济学家的专家评分更高的技术社会科学研究设计——这是我们新的自由系统评估 SnyderBench 的发现，其中我们有博士专家对人工智能模型的研究提案与哈佛大学政治经济学家吉姆·斯奈德 (Jim Snyder
viral_posts.full_text_en:
Frontier models can now propose technical social science research designs that experts grade more highly than the world's top political economist's---that's the finding from our new Free Systems eval, SnyderBench, in which we have PhD experts blind grade research proposals from AI models compared to papers written by Harvard political economist Jim Snyder (which the experts have not previously read). 

At the same time, we see no evidence that models can develop research ideas that experts rate as better overall contributions. They're getting better and better at the technical part of research, but not necessarily at the more subjective part.

This could be because human experts possess "judgment" that the models do not. 

It could also be that research "contribution" is so subjective that it doesn't actually point at any meaningful goal---consistent with this possibility, we find that our human experts don't agree with one another when rating project ideas for the strength of their contribution, with agreement rates barely higher than random chance. Perhaps social science research is what @alexolegimas might call a "relational good": something people value in part because it's produced by a human. We're not sure. 

This past January, I released the results of a pilot in which I had Claude Code replicate and extend a past empirical paper on vote-by-mail. 10 months later, it's stunning the amount of progress that's been made. It's no longer interesting to ask whether AI can collect data and run analyses automagically---we take that for granted---instead, the question is how much of the entire research loop AI can complete. Our tentative answer: AI can handle the technical aspects of empirical political economy research from end to end, devising the design and executing it, but for now, we still need humans to drive the agenda. 

This is joint work with @AndyCWMyers, and is of course dedicated to my PhD advisor Jim Snyder, who remains the world's great empirical political economist, AI or no AI. 

Lots more in the full piece here:

https://t.co/zgScGvp9EY
viral_posts.full_text_zh:
前沿模型现在可以提出比世界顶级政治经济学家的专家评分更高的技术社会科学研究设计——这是我们新的自由系统评估 SnyderBench 的发现，其中我们有博士专家对人工智能模型的研究提案与哈佛大学政治经济学家吉姆·斯奈德 (Jim Snyder) 撰写的论文（专家之前没有阅读过）进行了盲评。

与此同时，我们没有看到任何证据表明模型可以提出专家认为总体贡献更好的研究思路。他们在研究的技术部分越来越好，但在更主观的部分却不一定。

这可能是因为人类专家拥有模型所没有的“判断力”。

也可能是研究“贡献”是如此主观，以至于它实际上并没有指向任何有意义的目标——与这种可能性相一致，我们发现我们的人类专家在对项目想法的贡献强度进行评级时彼此不一致，一致率仅略高于随机机会。也许社会科学研究就是 @alexolegimas 所说的“关系善”：人们之所以重视它，部分原因是它是由人类产生的。我们不确定。

今年一月，我发布了一个试点结果，其中我让 Claude Code 复制并扩展了过去关于邮件投票的实证论文。 10 个月后，所取得的进展令人震惊。问人工智能是否可以自动收集数据并进行分析已经不再有趣了——我们认为这是理所当然的——相反，问题是人工智能可以完成整个研究循环的多少。我们的初步答案是：人工智能可以从头到尾处理实证政治经济学研究的技术方面，设计并执行它，但目前，我们仍然需要人类来推动议程。

这是与@AndyCWMyers 的联合工作，当然是献给我的博士生导师吉姆·斯奈德（Jim Snyder），无论人工智能与否，他仍然是世界上伟大的实证政治经济学家。

完整的内容还有更多内容：

今年一月，我发布了一个试点结果，其中我让 Claude Code 复制并扩展了过去关于邮件投票的实证论文。 10 个月后，所取得的进展令人震惊。问人工智能是否可以自动收集数据并进行分析已经不再有趣了——我们认为这是理所当然的——相反，问题是人工智能可以完成整个研究循环的多少。我们的初步答案是：人工智能可以从头到尾处理实证政治经济学研究的技术方面，设计并执行它，但目前，我们仍然需要人类来推动议程。

这是与@AndyCWMyers 的联合工作，当然是献给我的博士生导师吉姆·斯奈德（Jim Snyder），无论人工智能与否，他仍然是世界上伟大的实证政治经济学家。

viral_posts.title: The next phase of the Motes ecosystem is getting closer, and community participation is about to become even more import
viral_posts.full_text_en:
The next phase of the Motes ecosystem is getting closer, and community participation is about to become even more important.

@meetmotes is preparing to launch the Motes Aura Points Testnet, introducing a points system that connects user activity with future allocation opportunities.

The idea is to make participation count. As users interact with the ecosystem and engage with its AI Agent infrastructure, their activity can contribute to earning Aura Points.

These points are designed to play a role in allocation opportunities, giving users another reason to stay active and explore what Motes is building.

What’s interesting is how this connects to the bigger vision: Genesis NFTs introduce ownership and access to dedicated AI Agents, while Aura creates another layer that rewards verified participation.

It’s not just about holding an NFT anymore. Being involved in the ecosystem could matter too.

Genesis first. $MOTES next.

The Aura Points Testnet is coming soon. Stay ready!

@meetmotes
viral_posts.full_text_zh:
Motes 生态系统的下一阶段越来越近，社区参与也将变得更加重要。

@meetmotes 正准备启动 Motes Aura 积分测试网，引入一个将用户活动与未来分配机会联系起来的积分系统。

我们的想法是让参与变得有价值。当用户与生态系统互动并与其人工智能代理基础设施互动时，他们的活动可以有助于赚取 Aura 积分。

这些积分旨在在分配机会中发挥作用，为用户提供另一个保持活跃并探索 Motes 正在构建的内容的理由。

有趣的是这如何与更大的愿景联系起来：Genesis NFT 引入了专用人工智能代理的所有权和访问权限，而 Aura 创建了另一层来奖励经过验证的参与。

这不再只是持有 NFT 了。参与生态系统也很重要。

创世第一。接下来是$MOTES。

Aura Points 测试网即将推出。做好准备！

@meetmotes
